profile_text.body:
NVIDIA is a publicly traded semiconductor and computing company founded in 1993 and headquartered in Santa Clara, CA. It trades on the public markets under the ticker NVDA and reported revenue of $215,938,000,000 for the fiscal year ending January 25, 2026, per its most recent 10-K filing. The company operates across hardware, software, and AI services, with a significant focus on GPU-accelerated computing.

On the AI software side, NVIDIA offers the Nemotron family of multimodal foundation models, which the company describes as built for long-running, self-evolving agents capable of reasoning, multimodal vision, retrieval-augmented generation, speech, and safety tasks. The site describes Nemotron models as truly open source, with NVIDIA publishing training datasets, techniques, and model weights under the NVIDIA Open Model License, a permissive license that allows use, modification, distribution, and commercial deployment without requiring attribution to NVIDIA. Specific models in the family include NVIDIA Nemotron 3.5 Lightning, and the site notes support for NVIDIA RTX PRO and NVIDIA DGX Spark hardware platforms. Bryan Catanzaro, VP of applied deep learning research at NVIDIA, is cited on the site discussing the vision behind Nemotron.

NVIDIA also offers NIM, a set of inference microservices for deploying foundation models in enterprise environments, available at build.nvidia.com and requiring an NVIDIA AI Enterprise license for full production use. Additional tooling mentioned on the site includes NVIDIA NeMo for custom agentic AI development, NVIDIA Dynamo, TensorRT-LLM, and NVIDIA Blueprints for reference workflow acceleration. The held facts record no litigation or MCP server presence for the company at this time.
